expectations.evidence: 'On this record the buyer has capacity for this deal'.

expectations.text: Does not lower the capacity finding, or require experience, because the buyer has no track record

expectations.evidence: Account holder, letter date and limits, who signed the resolution vs operating agreement.
'$1.8M headroom before closing costs and deposit, which are not in the record.'

'Answer the track-record question plainly: none, and here is the verified money and authority.' Authority is described as verified, but the record gives only a signed resolution, which the response itself tags 'REPORTED to me as signed; I have not read it' and lists under 'Verify first'. Narrow, single-phrase trigger.

The two quoted 'Can say out loud' lines ('Counsel authenticated the bank letter directly with the bank. It shows $9M available against a $7.2M all-cash price, with no lender in the path.' / 'The managing member is the authorized signatory by signed resolution.') are supported by the record. The 'verified ... authority' phrase is paraphrased guidance, graded under C2.
No contract dates or remedies asserted; 'That reading is counsel's.'

format_checks.evidence: 'Next action: Confirm the letter names the LLC that will take title as the account holder and note the letter's date — your counsel.'
VERIFIED by counsel / REPORTED tags on each evidence item (one lapse: 'verified money and authority', see C2).
Ends with 'Work record: Evidence checked: none beyond your message | Calculations run: funds vs. price'.
$1.8M stated once; the $9M/$7.2M inputs recur only inside the quoted line.
'Account holder on the letter ... → tells us whether the money is already the buyer's, or whether a member still has to fund the entity before closing.'

notes: Otherwise clean; the C2 trigger rests on one phrase that upgrades reported signing authority to 'verified', contradicting its own tag. It is the closest call in the set.
